data.title: The courtyard through the window

memoryNodes.cue: Lin can see an enclosed open space below.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 林能看到下方围合的露天空间。

memoryNodes.cue: People can reach the finished wing without using stairs.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 人们可以不走楼梯到达已完成的翼楼。

memoryNodes.cue: The lines show how water leaves the building.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 线条显示水怎样离开建筑。

data.situation:
Lin followed the finished corridor to the corner by the window. Below it was a courtyard, enclosed by the west wing on three sides. The elevator stood opposite the stairs. On the wall, a rooftop photograph showed the courtyard from above, with lines marking where rainwater would go. The visit ended here, beside a model of the drainage system. Lin: Can a wheelchair user reach the exhibition without using the stairs?
Jo: Yes. This completed wing is accessible by elevator. The map at the desk shows the route.
Lin: And these lines on the rooftop picture?
Jo: They lead to the drainage model. The plan shows where water leaves the roof and the courtyard.
Lin: I can see how the same building has different routes for people and water. After the visit
Lin returned her leaflet to the desk. Before leaving, she checked the route from the elevator to the courtyard door: turn at the corner, follow the corridor, then look for the window overlooking the canal. She would need to explain that route to visitors during her next shift.

readingBlocks.zh:
林：轮椅使用者不用楼梯也能到展览吗？
乔：能，这部分已完成的翼楼可乘电梯到达。前台地图标出了路线。
林：屋顶照片上的线呢？
乔：通向排水模型，计划显示水怎样离开屋顶和庭院。
林：我看明白了，同一栋建筑里，人和水走不同的路线。

readingBlocks.en:
After the visit
Lin returned her leaflet to the desk. Before leaving, she checked the route from the elevator to the courtyard door: turn at the corner, follow the corridor, then look for the window overlooking the canal. She would need to explain that route to visitors during her next shift.
readingBlocks.zh:
参观之后
林把介绍页送回前台。离开前，她核对从电梯到庭院门的路线：在转角转弯，沿走廊前行，再找俯瞰运河的窗户。下次轮班，她需要向访客解释这条路。

glossary.zh: 连接建筑内房间的长通道；走廊
glossary.note: 可数空间名词，along/down a corridor。
glossary.example: Lin follows the corridor to the window.

externalEvidence.definition: an enclosed passageway; rooms usually open onto it

glossary.zh: 两边或两面相交处；转角
glossary.note: at the corner；本例建筑内部转角。
glossary.example: Turn at the corner beside the window.

externalEvidence.definition: an interior angle formed by two meeting walls

glossary.zh: 由墙或建筑围合的露天场地；庭院
glossary.note: 可数名词；本例为建筑围合的空间。

externalEvidence.definition: an area wholly or partly surrounded by walls or buildings

glossary.zh: 在楼层间运送人员或货物的电梯
glossary.example: The elevator stands opposite the stairs.

externalEvidence.definition: lifting device consisting of a platform or cage that is raised and lowered mechanically in a vertical shaft in order to move people from one floor to another in a building

glossary.zh: 能够进入或到达的；可通达的
glossary.note: accessible to wheelchair users/by elevator；具体说明可达方式。
glossary.example: The exhibition wing is accessible by elevator.
glossary.exampleZh: 展览翼楼可以乘电梯到达。

externalEvidence.label: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: The physical access sense is selected; the scene names the actual means of access.

glossary.example: The rooftop photograph shows the courtyard from above.
glossary.exampleZh: 屋顶拍摄的照片从上方显示庭院。

externalEvidence.definition: the top of a (usually flat) roof

glossary.zh: 排走积水的设施系统；排水系统
glossary.example: The model shows the drainage system.

externalEvidence.label: Cambridge Dictionary · drainage system
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: The drainage/system entries and collocation support the network of connected drainage devices, distinct from a process-only local WordNet gloss.

externalEvidence.label: Collins Dictionary · drainage system
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: The drainage entry includes system as well as process; the selected teaching use is the system.
